questions.q: How old was Umar bin Al-Khattab when he embraced Islam?
questions.explain: Umar was a sturdy young man of 25 or 26.

questions.q: Which surah did Umar hear from behind the Kaaba's covering?
questions.explain: Umar slipped behind the cloth of the Kaaba and was spellbound hearing Al-Haqqah.

questions.q: Who told Umar about his sister's belief in order to stop him?
questions.explain: Nu'aym hid his Islam and told Umar so that he would not kill the Prophet SAW.

questions.q: How did Umar feel when he accidentally struck his sister until she bled?
questions.explain: Umar was ashamed and sorry, and wanted to read the pages his sister had been reading.
Reciting Taha changed Umar, who had wanted to kill the Prophet SAW.

questions.q: Where did Umar pronounce the shahada?
questions.explain: Umar became a Muslim before the Prophet SAW at Dar al-Arqam.

questions.q: What does Al-Faruq, Umar's title, mean?
options: The one who separates truth from falsehood
questions.explain: Al-Faruq was Umar's title from the Prophet SAW.

questions.q: Who led the two rows of Muslims to the Kaaba to pray openly?
questions.explain: Two rows led by Hamzah and Umar moved to the Kaaba.

questions.q: The first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah are the days Allah loves most of the year.
questions.explain: True. The ustaz reminded of this at the start of the lecture.

questions.q: Umar began to change when he heard the Prophet SAW's recitation himself, not just what others said.
questions.explain: True. Do not quarrel without understanding. Listen for yourself first.

questions.q: Put these events in the right order.
questions.explain: Umar heard Al-Haqqah, was stopped by Nu'aym, struck his sister, read Taha, then pronounced the shahada.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: The successor leader of the Prophet SAW

questions.explain: Dhul-Hijjah is the month of Hajj, Al-Haqqah is the 69th surah, sha'ir is poetry, and a khalifah is the Prophet's successor.

questions.q: Someone seems impossible to ever accept the truth. What lesson does Umar's story give?
options: Guidance is only for the poor
Guidance is not impossible, he could become a pillar of Islam
questions.explain: Someone who seems impossible to embrace Islam can become a strengthener of Islam.
